## Warm-up 🔥 {.smaller}

⏱️ 5 min · with dplyr

```r
library(dplyr)
seqs <- read.csv("data/samples.csv")
```

Per `organism`: how many samples, and the mean `length`? 🤔

::: notes
0–5 min. group_by(organism) |> summarise(n = n(), mean_length = mean(length)).
We'll plot exactly this later in the block.
:::

## The idea: a plot is built in layers 🧱 {.smaller}

Every ggplot has 3 parts:

| Part | Question | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **data** | which table? | `seqs` |
| **aes** (aesthetics) | which column goes **where**? | x = length, y = gc_content |
| **geom** | which **shape**? | points, bars, boxes |

. . .

```r
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(seqs, aes(x = length, y = gc_content)) +
  geom_point()
```

. . .

Layers are added with **`+`** (not `|>`!) ➕

::: notes
5–12 min. Draw it as a recipe: data → map columns → choose a shape.
The + vs |> mix-up is the #1 error of the block.
:::

## Four plots you will actually use 📊 {.smaller}

```r
ggplot(seqs, aes(x = gc_content)) + geom_histogram(bins = 15)    # distribution
ggplot(seqs, aes(x = length, y = gc_content)) + geom_point()     # relationship
ggplot(seqs, aes(x = organism, y = gc_content)) + geom_boxplot() # compare groups
ggplot(seqs, aes(x = organism)) + geom_bar()                     # count per group
```

. . .

Same plots as `hist()`, `plot()`, `boxplot()` last class, and matplotlib before that 🔁

::: notes
12–20 min. Run all four live. geom_bar counts rows itself, no group_by needed.
:::

## Colour = another column 🎨 {.smaller}

Inside `aes()`, colour is **data**:

```r
ggplot(seqs, aes(x = length, y = gc_content, colour = organism)) +
  geom_point(size = 3)
```

. . .

Outside `aes()`, colour is just **style**:

```r
ggplot(seqs, aes(x = gc_content)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 15, fill = "steelblue")
```

. . .

The legend appears **automatically** ✨

::: notes
20–25 min. Rule of thumb: depends on a column → inside aes(); fixed value → outside.
:::

## Labels & a clean look 🏷️ {.smaller}

```r
ggplot(seqs, aes(x = length, y = gc_content, colour = organism)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(title  = "GC content vs sequence length",
       x      = "Length (bp)",
       y      = "GC content (%)",
       colour = "Organism") +
  theme_minimal()
```

. . .

Small multiples: one panel per group 🪟

```r
  + facet_wrap(~ organism)
```

::: notes
25–30 min. Try theme_bw(), theme_classic() too. facet_wrap is a ggplot superpower, matplotlib needs subplots for this.
:::

## dplyr → ggplot2 🤝 {.smaller}

Summarise first, then plot the summary:

```r
seqs |>
  group_by(organism) |>
  summarise(mean_length = mean(length)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = organism, y = mean_length)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Mean length per organism", x = "Organism", y = "Mean length (bp)")
```

. . .

`|>` until the table is ready, then **`+`** for the layers ⚠️

::: notes
30–35 min. geom_col = bars with heights from the data; geom_bar = counts rows.
:::

## Saving 💾 {.smaller}

```r
p <- ggplot(seqs, aes(x = gc_content)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 15)

ggsave("results/gc_histogram.png", p, width = 8, height = 5)
```

. . .

No `png()` … `dev.off()` this time 🙌

::: notes
35–37 min. width/height in inches by default.
:::

## Exercise: three plots 🖼️ {.smaller}

⏱️ 35 min · breakout rooms · pairs · file: **`scripts/plots.R`**

Use `data/samples.csv` (or **your own project data** 🎯):

1. 📊 Histogram of `gc_content`, filled with a colour of your choice
2. ⚫ Scatter plot `length` vs `gc_content`, **coloured by** `organism`
3. 📦 Bar chart of **mean** `length` per organism (dplyr → `geom_col`)
4. Every plot: title + axis labels (`labs()`) + a theme
5. Save all three with `ggsave()` into `results/`

💡 **Bonus:** add `facet_wrap(~ organism)` to the scatter plot

**Commit** 💾 `plots.R` (not the PNGs 🙈)

::: notes
37–75 min. Common issues: |> instead of + (error "could not find function geom_point" or weird pipe errors),
colour outside aes() with a column name, results/ folder missing.
:::

## Wrap-up ✅ {.smaller}

```r
ggplot(data, aes(x = ..., y = ..., colour = ...)) +   # what & where
  geom_point() +                                     # which shape
  labs(title = ..., x = ..., y = ...) +               # labels
  theme_minimal()                                    # look
ggsave("results/plot.png")                           # save
```
